methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $235M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Transportation (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Electra.aero is a Series B transportation company founded by John Langford that has raised $235M to date. The relevant peer universe consists of 7 private transportation companies—including Rivian, The Boring Company, Einride, Arc Boats, and Parallel Systems—with no public comparables available.

Stage-progression methodology is applicable here. Using total capital raised ($235M) as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 1.9x step-up multiplier from Series B to the subsequent funding round yields an implied valuation of $446M. Peer-median triangulation is not applicable; while 3 same-sector peers exist in Transportation, none meet the filtering criteria of same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation-tier comparability. A broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $380M (low) to $513M (high), with a median point of $446M. This single-method result carries material uncertainty given reliance on stage-progression mechanics rather than market-comparable validation. The key unresolved variable is whether Electra.aero's capital efficiency and unit economics align with prior-stage funding rounds, or whether market conditions and investor appetite have shifted materially since the last fundraise. Absent a sufficiently dense peer dataset at comparable stage and sector, investors should treat this range as illustrative rather than definitive, and conduct primary diligence on unit metrics and market positioning.
